verses.1: And the LORD spoke to Moses by the Red Sea, in the second year after they had left Egypt. It was the first month of their journey.
verses.2: And the children of Israel will celebrate Passover on that day.
verses.3: On the forty-second day of this month, in the evening, it shall be done according to all its laws and regulations.
verses.4: And Moses spoke to the children of Israel about what they should do during the Passover.
verses.5: They observed the Passover on the first day of the month, after fourteen days. They did this between the two evenings in the land of Canaan. This was in accordance with all that Jehovah commanded Moses. Thus did the children of Israel do.
verses.6: And there were people who were spiritually impure, and they were unable to perform the Passover ceremony on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron on that day.
verses.7: And those people said to him, “We are impure in our hearts. Why should we go ahead and offer our sacrifices to Jehovah on the day of his appointed time, among the children of Israel?”
verses.8: And Moses said to them, “Stand still. Let us hear what Jehovah commands you.”
verses.9: And Jehovah spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.10: And he said to the children of Israel, “Each person should be careful that no one becomes unclean either in their own home or in any other place where they live. They must also celebrate Passover as commanded by God.”
verses.11: In the second month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between evening and night, it will be eaten with spices and aromatics.
verses.12: They shall not leave it until evening. In no way shall they break it down, as is required by the laws of Passover. They must carry out these procedures accordingly.
verses.13: And the man who was unclean, and who did not follow the proper ways, stopped from performing the sacrifices. His soul was marked as unclean by his people, because Jehovah did not accept his sins at that time.
verses.14: And just as a farmer lives among you and prepares Passover according to its laws and traditions, so too shall there be one law for you, for the farmer, and for all who live in this land.
verses.15: And on the day he built the tabernacle, the cloud covered it, making it a holy place. In the evening, there would be fire on top of the tabernacle, until nightfall.
verses.16: And always, the clouds will cover us, and it will look like fire during the night.
verses.17: And when the cloud rises above the tabernacle, then the children of Israel will go there. And in the place where the cloud stays, there will also be a place for the children of Israel to rest.
verses.18: By the Lord, the children of Israel will go forth. By the Lord, they will dwell wherever the cloud rests above the tabernacle.
verses.19: And in the days when the clouds covered the tent, the Israelites kept the covenant with Yahweh. They did not leave it behind.
verses.20: And there will be those clouds that will cover the tent during the days of judgment. They will dwell under Jehovah’s rule, and they will also be carried away by Jehovah’s power.
verses.21: And there will be a cloud that will stay up from evening until morning. The cloud will move from day to night, and we will travel with it, day and night.
verses.22: Or days, or months… When the clouds cover the tent. The children of Israel will stay there, and they will not go away. They will stay in that place during those days.
verses.23: By Jehovah they will be settled, and by Jehovah they will carry on the duty of keeping Jehovah’s covenant. They will do this under the leadership of Moses.
